text: I find that when you're busy, you're constantly just go, go, go, go. There's no time to do any deep thinking. Deep thinking takes time and space, and you got to create that space.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Lenny asks Alex about the power of forcing yourself to write and reflect versus not doing so. Alex explains why he dedicates time for deep reflection despite his busy schedule. He describes how he used to work from home on Fridays to avoid meetings and focus on strategic thinking - reading documents carefully and identifying what could have saved time during the week if he had done it beforehand.
text_ko: 바쁠 때는 계속 그냥 달려만 가게 되더라고요. 깊이 생각할 시간은 없어요. 깊이 생각하려면 시간과 공간이 필요한데, 그 여유를 스스로 만들어줘야 해요.
text_zh: 我发现当你很忙的时候，就是不停地冲冲冲，根本没时间深入思考什么。深度思考是需要时间和空间的，你得主动给自己创造这个空间。
text_es: Me doy cuenta de que cuando andas súper ocupado, es puro correr y correr sin parar. No hay tiempo para pensar las cosas a fondo. Para reflexionar en serio necesitas tiempo y espacio, y ese espacio lo tienes que crear tú mismo.
key_sentence: Create space to reflect and luxuriate in deep thinking.
original_text: I find that when you're busy, you're constantly just go, go, go, go. There's no time to do any deep thinking. Deep thinking takes time and space, and you got to create that space. The mundane, pointless bullshit will take every square inch you give it. So you got to make that space to sit back and reflect and luxuriate in these ideas.

vocabulary.definition: A cognitive process that involves thorough analysis and contemplation of complex ideas or problems, often leading to innovative solutions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, deep thinking is crucial for strategic planning, problem-solving, and fostering creativity, allowing leaders to develop comprehensive insights and long-term visions.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a level of thoughtfulness that goes beyond surface-level analysis, often requiring uninterrupted time and mental space to explore ideas fully.

text: I think LLMs are truly a disruptive technology. In fact, I would argue that what we're seeing in the industry is us trying to use mature playbooks from the end stage of the last tech era in one that doesn't really fit yet.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Lenny asks Alex how LLMs and generative AI will change how products are built in the next 3-5 years. Alex argues that LLMs fundamentally disrupt existing assumptions about software development costs and capabilities. He explains that the industry is mistakenly applying old strategies to this new paradigm, comparing LLMs to 'magical duct tape' that bridges human intelligence and traditional computing.
text_ko: 저는 대형 언어 모델(LLMs)이 정말 파괴적 기술(disruptive technology)이라고 생각해요. 사실 저는 업계에서 지금 보이는 게, 우리가 지난 기술 시대 말기에 쓰이던 성숙한 플레이북(mature playbooks)을 지금의 상황에 그대로 적용하려고 하는 건데, 그게 아직 잘 맞지 않는다고 주장하고 싶어요.
text_zh: 我觉得大语言模型(LLMs)真的是颠覆性技术。其实我认为，现在整个行业的问题在于，我们还在用上一个技术时代末期那套成熟的打法，但这套东西在新时代根本不适用。
text_es: Creo que los LLM son realmente una tecnología disruptiva. De hecho, yo diría que lo que estamos viendo en la industria es que estamos tratando de usar estrategias que ya funcionaban al final de la era tecnológica anterior en una que todavía no encaja bien.
key_sentence: LLMs are truly a disruptive technology.
original_text: I think LLMs are truly a disruptive technology. In fact, I would argue that what we're seeing in the industry is us trying to use mature playbooks from the end stage of the last tech era in one that doesn't really fit yet. To me, LLMs are magical duct tape. They're formed principally by the distilled intuition of all of society into a thing that operates between, a cost structure between human and plain old computing.

vocabulary.definition: Causing significant change or upheaval in an industry or market, often through innovation or new technologies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'disruptive' refers to innovations that create new markets or value networks, ultimately displacing established market leaders and products.
vocabulary.nuance: While often viewed positively in terms of innovation, 'disruptive' can also carry a negative connotation when it implies chaos or instability.

vocabulary.definition: Established strategies or frameworks that have been tested and refined over time, typically used for guiding decision-making and operations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'mature playbooks' refer to proven methodologies that organizations rely on to navigate complex challenges and ensure successful outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'mature playbooks' suggest reliability, they may also imply rigidity, potentially hindering adaptability in rapidly changing environments.

text: In this cacophony, how do you stand out? You stand out by having good taste. I think taste is the most important thing. You have a perspective that is different from the background noise, different from the average and that people find compelling.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Lenny asks about skills product managers should develop as AI changes the landscape. Alex discusses how AI has reduced the cost of information production, creating overwhelming amounts of content. He argues that in this environment of information overload, developing distinctive taste and perspective becomes the key differentiator rather than just executing standard playbooks.
text_ko: 이런 소음 속에서 어떻게 돋보이나요? 좋은 안목(taste)을 갖추면 돋보여요. 저는 안목이 가장 중요하다고 생각해요. 주변의 잡음이나 평균과는 다른, 사람들이 끌리는 관점을 갖추는 거예요.
text_zh: 在这种嘈杂的环境下，你怎么脱颖而出呢？靠的就是品味。我觉得品味是最重要的。你得有自己的观点，不能跟风，不能平庸，要让人觉得有意思、有吸引力。
text_es: En medio de tanto ruido, ¿cómo te destacas? Te destacas teniendo buen gusto. Para mí el gusto es lo más importante. Tienes que tener una perspectiva que sea distinta a todo ese ruido de fondo, distinta al promedio, y que la gente encuentre atractiva.
key_sentence: Stand out in this cacophony by leaning into your taste.
original_text: In this cacophony, how do you stand out? You stand out by having good taste. I think taste is the most important thing. You have a perspective that is different from the background noise, different from the average and that people find compelling. How do you find your own taste and how do you lean into that taste is, I think, much more important than just generically executing in the way that everybody else could do.

vocabulary.definition: Evoking interest, attention, or admiration in a powerful way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a compelling product or idea is one that captures the interest of consumers or investors, often leading to increased sales or funding.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'compelling' suggests strong attraction, it can imply a sense of urgency or necessity that may not always be present.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of considering something, often shaped by personal experiences or context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, having a unique perspective can differentiate a company’s strategy and innovation, allowing it to stand out in a competitive market.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a depth of understanding that goes beyond surface-level observations, making it valuable in strategic discussions.

vocabulary.definition: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds, often used metaphorically to describe a chaotic environment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a cacophony can refer to the overwhelming noise of competing ideas or messages in the marketplace, making it challenging for brands to communicate effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'cacophony' typically has a negative connotation, it can also be used to describe a vibrant, dynamic environment when contextually appropriate.

text: So much of the way that we tackle problems and build products is this builder mindset. It's like I have a plan. I then manipulate things to match my plan and make it happen. And this is a way you can create tons of value.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Alex introduces his core philosophy of 'gardening versus building' as an alternative approach to product development and problem-solving. The builder mindset involves creating detailed plans and forcing execution, while the gardening mindset focuses on nurturing things that can grow organically with minimal intervention. Alex argues this gardening approach can create exponentially more value than the linear effort-to-value relationship of traditional building.
text_ko: 우리가 문제를 해결하고 제품을 만드는 방식의 많은 부분이 빌더 마인드셋(builder mindset)이에요. '계획이 있으니 그 계획에 맞게 이것저것 조정해서 실현한다'는 식이죠. 이런 방식으로 엄청난 가치를 만들어낼 수 있어요.
text_zh: 我们解决问题和做产品的思路，很大程度上都是这种建造者思维(builder mindset)。就是我先有个计划，然后想办法让现实配合我的计划，推动事情发生。用这种方式确实能创造很大的价值。
text_es: Gran parte de cómo abordamos los problemas y desarrollamos productos viene de esta mentalidad de constructor (builder mindset). Es como que tengo un plan, entonces manejo las cosas para que encajen con mi plan y lo hago realidad. Y así es como puedes generar muchísimo valor.
key_sentence: So much of the way that we tackle problems and build products is this builder mindset.
original_text: So much of the way that we tackle problems and build products is this builder mindset. It's like I have a plan. I then manipulate things to match my plan and make it happen. And this is a way you can create tons of value. Part of the problem though is it can't possibly create more value than the effort that you put into it. What I look for instead are things that can be gardened, things that can grow on their own and that you can direct or maybe give a little bit of extra energy to or curate over, and is a totally different mindset for it.

vocabulary.definition: A builder mindset refers to a proactive and innovative approach to problem-solving and product development, characterized by a willingness to experiment and iterate.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, a builder mindset is essential for entrepreneurs and teams to create effective solutions and adapt to changing market demands.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a positive attitude towards challenges, emphasizing creativity and resilience rather than a fixed or rigid approach.

vocabulary.definition: To manipulate means to skillfully handle, control, or influence something or someone, often with a specific goal in mind.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, manipulation can refer to adjusting variables, processes, or resources to achieve desired outcomes, such as optimizing workflows or influencing market perceptions.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'manipulate' can have negative connotations of deceit or coercion, in a business setting it can also imply strategic and skillful management.

text: If you do this properly, it looks like magic. I've been told that this is completely against all the advice that people get, including products nowadays, but I think it's a very powerful approach that works in a lot of different contexts.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Lenny asks Alex to elaborate on the gardening versus building concept and provide examples. Alex explains that when you focus on nurturing things with compounding potential rather than forcing predetermined outcomes, the results can appear magical. He describes this as 'farming for miracles' - planting many seeds knowing that while you can't predict which will succeed, the probability is high that at least one will grow into something transformative.
text_ko: 이걸 제대로 하면 마치 마법처럼 보여요. 요즘 사람들이 받는 조언들—제품(products) 관련 조언까지 포함해서—모두와 완전히 반대된다고들 말하더라고요. 그래도 저는 이 방법이 여러 맥락에서 아주 강력하게 통한다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 如果你把这个做到位了，看起来就像变魔术一样。我知道现在很多人都说这完全违背了常规建议，包括产品方面的建议，但我觉得这个方法特别有效，而且适用于很多不同的场景。
text_es: Si lo haces bien, parece magia. Me han dicho que esto va totalmente en contra de todos los consejos que recibe la gente, incluso con los productos de hoy en día, pero creo que es un enfoque muy poderoso que funciona en muchas situaciones diferentes.
key_sentence: I think it's a very powerful approach that works in a lot of different contexts.
original_text: If you do this properly, it looks like magic. I've been told that this is completely against all the advice that people get, including products nowadays, but I think it's a very powerful approach that works in a lot of different contexts. You're farming for miracles. And so on a systemic basis, I can't tell you which of these things will work, but I can tell you there's a very high likelihood that one of these will work in a way that is interesting and transformative.

vocabulary.definition: Having great power or strength; capable of producing significant effects or results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'powerful' often describes strategies, tools, or leaders that have a strong impact on performance and outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'powerful' conveys strength, it can also imply a sense of influence or authority that may not always be positive.

vocabulary.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem; a method or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, an 'approach' refers to the specific tactics or methodologies employed to achieve goals or solve issues.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a systematic or thoughtful method, and is often used in discussions about innovation or problem-solving.

text: The kayfabe, the thing that everyone pretends to believe is true, is obviously incorrect. And the dangerous part about this is it can lead you to make very bad decisions.
speaker: Alex Komoroske
context: Lenny asks Alex to explain organizational kayfabe - a concept borrowed from professional wrestling meaning something everyone knows is fake but acts like it's real. Alex describes how small optimistic lies compound up through organizational layers, creating strategies that are obviously flawed but become dangerous to challenge. He explains the dilemma faced by employees who see the truth but risk career damage by speaking up.
text_ko: 사람들이 모두 진짜라고 믿는 척하는 케이페이브(kayfabe)는 분명히 잘못된 거예요. 더 위험한 건, 그 때문에 아주 나쁜 결정을 내릴 수 있다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 大家心照不宣地装作相信的那套说辞，明显是错的。最危险的地方就在于，这会让你做出很糟糕的决定。
text_es: El teatro corporativo, esa cosa que todos fingimos que es verdad, obviamente está mal. Y lo peligroso de esto es que te puede llevar a tomar decisiones muy malas.
key_sentence: the dangerous part about this is it can lead you to make very bad decisions.
original_text: The kayfabe, the thing that everyone pretends to believe is true, is obviously incorrect. And the dangerous part about this is it can lead you to make very bad decisions. And if you as someone who sees this can see that wait a second, the official strategy is definitely not going to work, you're like, 'I got to tell somebody. We're doing work that's going in a bad direction. It's not going to work.'

vocabulary.definition: Decisions are choices made after considering various options and their potential outcomes. They often involve weighing risks and benefits to arrive at a conclusion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, decisions are critical as they can affect strategy, operations, and overall success; they are often made based on data analysis and market research.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'decisions' carries a weight of responsibility, implying that the outcomes can significantly impact stakeholders and the organization as a whole.
